newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban offer amnesty to Afghan government troops.
newsitem.headline: Taleban offer amnesty to Afghan government troops.

text.p: The Taleban militia occupying Kabul have declared an amnesty for Afghan government soldiers and officers who surrender, a commander for the triumphant rebels said.

"We have declared a general amnesty for all government soldiers and officers if they give up their guns. Taleban will not take revenge. We have no personal rancour. If the people find someone responsible for crimes in the past we will judge him according to Islamic law," a Taleban commander, named only Musa, told Reuters.

Musa said Taleban fighters had occupied Afghan army headquarters in the northern suburb of Khairkhana, which was headquarters of government commander General Baba Jan. He said Taleban forces were heading north from the Bagram airbase they captured last night. "We know the senior government leaders escaped from Kabul to the north," he said.
Musa said the Jabal-us-Seraj base further north was still held by the government's top commander Ahmad Shah Masood but Taleban fighters were heading in that direction.
Musa said Taleban used loudspeakers to tell civilians in Kabul to go about their daily life as usual.

He said he hoped the situation would stabilise and result in better food supplies although hundreds of thousands of civilians in Kabul would remain vulnerable, particularly in the coming winter. He added that the World Food Programme had received a convoy of 30 trucks of food from Mazar-i-Sharif, north-west of Kabul, last night.
